# FishTool in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/struct.FishTool.html

## Expand description

A single fish shell function dependency declared in `[tool.fish.<name>]`.

The TOML key (`<name>`) is the fish function name to check. Unlike
[ CargoTool](https://docs.rs/struct.CargoTool.html) and

[, there is no](https://docs.rs/struct.OsTool.html)

`OsTool``check` or `install` command —
the presence check is always `fish -c "functions --query <name>"`, which
covers user-defined functions, autoloaded functions, and builtins. When the
function is absent the run aborts with the requirement and any `hint`.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.hint)

`hint: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>An optional message describing how to define the function, shown when it
is absent (e.g. `"define my_fn in ~/.config/fish/functions/my_fn.fish"`).

# UpdateRecord in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/struct.UpdateRecord.html

## Expand description

A tool install or version update that occurred during a run.

Collected by the run machinery and returned in [`RunReport::updates`]; the
binaries print a consolidated summary after the final `Runtime` line.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.name)

`name: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The tool’s name (e.g. `"cargo-nextest"` or `"cargo-rake"` for the
self-update).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.from)

`from: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>The version that was present before the update, or `None` when the tool
was not previously installed.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.to)

`to: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>The version now installed, or `None` when the post-install version was
not determined (fresh installs via `cargo install` do not re-probe).

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

}## Expand description

Errors that can occur while loading, validating, or running a `Rakefile.toml`.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Io)

### Io([Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html))

The `Rakefile.toml` could not be read from disk.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Parse)

### Parse([Error](https://docs.rs/toml/1.1.2+spec-1.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/toml/de/error/struct.Error.html))

The `Rakefile.toml` contents could not be parsed (covers a command
missing its `name` or `cmd`).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyTarget)

### EmptyTarget

A target defined neither commands nor dependencies.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyCmd)

### EmptyCmd

A target’s command declared a `cmd` with no program to run.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MissingCommandBody)

### MissingCommandBody

A target’s command declared no body at all — none of `cmd`, `sh`, `fish`,
or `ps`.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AmbiguousCommandBody)

### AmbiguousCommandBody

A target’s command declared both a `cmd` array and a shell variant; the
two kinds are mutually exclusive.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyShell)

### EmptyShell

A target’s command declared a shell variant that is empty or only whitespace.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MissingShellVariant)

### MissingShellVariant

A command was selected to run but declares no variant for the detected shell, so there is nothing to run under it.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPlatform)

### InvalidPlatform

A command’s `platform` list named an unrecognized token (likely a typo).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidArch)

### InvalidArch

A command’s `arch` list named an unrecognized token (likely a typo).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyPlatformList)

### EmptyPlatformList

A command declared an empty `platform` or `arch` list, which would gate
the command out on every host.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPlatformVariant)

### InvalidPlatformVariant

A `[target.X.KEY]` table key that is neither a known base field
(`command`/`depends_on`/`tools`) nor a recognized platform/family token.
The old `platform = [...]` field at the target level has been replaced by
platform-keyed sub-tables (e.g. `[target.X.linux]`).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TargetNotAvailableOnPlatform)

### TargetNotAvailableOnPlatform

The target exists in the Rakefile but only as platform-specific variants
(`[target.X.linux]`, etc.) and none of them match the current host.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DuplicateCommand)

### DuplicateCommand

A target declared two commands with the same `name`.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownTarget)

### UnknownTarget

A target was requested that does not exist in the `Rakefile.toml`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownDependency)

### UnknownDependency

A target’s `depends_on` referenced a target that does not exist.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ConflictingDependency)

### ConflictingDependency

A target’s `depends_on` lists the same name both as a regular dependency
and as a skip entry (with a `^` prefix), which is contradictory.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CircularDependency)

### CircularDependency

The dependency graph contains a cycle.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SkipNotAllowed)

### SkipNotAllowed

A target requested to be skipped (e.g. `^clean`) is depended on by
another target that still runs in this invocation, so skipping it would
run that target without its prerequisite.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Spawn)

### Spawn

A target’s program could not be launched.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownTool)

### UnknownTool

A target’s `tools` listed a name with no matching `[tool.cargo.<name>]`
or `[tool.os.<name>]` entry.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownCommandTool)

### UnknownCommandTool

A command’s `tools` listed a name with no matching tool entry in any
category (`[tool.cargo]`, `[tool.os]`, or `[tool.fish]`).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ToolDeclaredAtBothLevels)

### ToolDeclaredAtBothLevels

A tool name appears in both the target’s `tools` list and a command’s
`tools` list within the same target — declare it at one level only.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyToolCommand)

### EmptyToolCommand

A tool’s `check` or `install` command was declared empty.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ToolUpdateMissingCrate)

### ToolUpdateMissingCrate

A tool set `update = true` under the `crates-io` semver check but did not
declare the `crate` needed to query crates.io.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ToolInstallSpawn)

### ToolInstallSpawn

A tool’s `install` program could not be launched.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ToolInstallFailed)

### ToolInstallFailed

A tool’s `install` command ran but exited non-zero.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RequiredToolMissing)

### RequiredToolMissing

A required OS tool is not installed and declares no `install` command for
`rake` to run, so the run is aborted with the requirement (and any `hint`).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DuplicateTool)

### DuplicateTool

A tool name was declared in more than one of the `[tool.cargo]`,
`[tool.os]`, or `[tool.fish]` categories; tool reference names share
one flat namespace.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SelfUpdatePrepare)

### SelfUpdatePrepare([Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html))

The running binary could not be renamed before a self-update install.

On Windows, `cargo install` cannot overwrite a running executable, so the
binary is renamed to `<exe>.bak` first. This error fires when that rename
fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RustToolchainMissing)

### RustToolchainMissing

A Rust toolchain (cargo) is required to run targets but none is available — it was not found and installation was declined, impossible (no interactive terminal), or did not make cargo available.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RustInstallSpawn)

### RustInstallSpawn

The rustup installer could not be launched.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RustInstallFailed)

### RustInstallFailed

The rustup installer ran but exited non-zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RustChannelMissing)

### RustChannelMissing

The requested Rust toolchain channel is not installed and installing it was declined or impossible (no interactive terminal).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidToolchain)

### InvalidToolchain

The top-level `toolchain` value is empty or contains whitespace.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidLifecycleAddress)

### InvalidLifecycleAddress

The `[lifecycle]` table’s `address` value does not parse as a
`host:port` socket address.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LicenseMalformed)

### LicenseMalformed

A license key string is not in the expected format, or its encoding or cryptographic bytes are invalid.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LicenseInvalidSignature)

### LicenseInvalidSignature

A license key’s signature did not verify — the key may have been tampered with or was signed by a different authority.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LicenseExpired)

### LicenseExpired

The license key’s expiry date has passed.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LicenseRemoveNoTerminal)

### LicenseRemoveNoTerminal

Stdin is not a terminal; cannot interactively confirm license removal.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.LicenseRemoveFailed)

### LicenseRemoveFailed([Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html))

A filesystem error occurred removing the stored license key file.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-RefUnwindSafe-for-Error)

        duration_ms: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    },
    CommandSkipped {
        run_id: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
        ts: [DateTime](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/datetime/struct.DateTime.html)<[Utc](https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/chrono/offset/utc/struct.Utc.html)>,

    },
    BeforeTool {

    },

        target: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
        command: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        tool: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
        outcome: [ToolOutcome](https://docs.rs/enum.ToolOutcome.html),
        from: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        to: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
        duration_ms: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html),
    },
    Unknown,
}## Expand description

A single lifecycle event, externally tagged so a JSON consumer can match
on the `"event"` field without a schema.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BeforeAll)

### BeforeAll

The whole run is about to start; the execution plan is already known.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AfterAll)

### AfterAll

The whole run has finished (successfully, or via a stopped chain).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BeforeTarget)

### BeforeTarget

A target is about to run (its dependencies have already run).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AfterTarget)

### AfterTarget

A target has finished running all of its commands (or stopped early).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TargetSkipped)

### TargetSkipped

A `^`-skipped target was pruned from the run instead of executing.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BeforeCommand)

### BeforeCommand

A command is about to be spawned.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AfterCommand)

### AfterCommand

A command finished (or failed to launch).

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CommandSkipped)

### CommandSkipped

A command was excluded by its `platform`/`arch` gate.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BeforeTool)

### BeforeTool

A tool is about to be checked/ensured.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AfterTool)

### AfterTool

A tool check/install/update has finished.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unknown)

### Unknown

A forward-compatibility catch-all: any `"event"` tag a consumer built
against an older version of this enum doesn’t recognize deserializes
here instead of failing the datagram. Never constructed or emitted by
this crate itself — `Deserialize`-only.

# detect_shell_family in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.detect_shell_family.html

`pub fn detect_shell_family() -> `[ShellFamily](https://docs.rs/enum.ShellFamily.html)## Expand description

Detect the current shell family from the process environment.

The detection follows a fixed priority order (first match wins):

- `RAKE_SHELL`env variable — set to any shell name (- `fish`,- `sh`,- `bash`,- `pwsh`, …) to pin the family, skipping all other detection.
- `POWERSHELL_DISTRIBUTION_CHANNEL`or- `PSModulePath`(non-Windows only) — checked before- `$SHELL`because PowerShell does not set- `$SHELL`.
- `FISH_VERSION`env variable — exported by fish to all child processes; checked before- `$SHELL`because- `$SHELL`reflects the login shell, not the running shell.
- `$SHELL`’s basename — classified into a- `ShellFamily`
- Platform default — `ShellFamily::Ps``ShellFamily::Posix`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use librake::{ShellFamily, detect_shell_family};
let family = detect_shell_family();
// key() returns "sh", "fish", or "ps" depending on the environment.
println!("shell: {}", family.key());
```

---

# ensure_rust_toolchain in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.ensure_rust_toolchain.html

## Expand description

Ensure the required Rust toolchain is available, then pin this run to it.

With `toolchain` `None` (no channel declared) this is a quiet no-op when
`cargo` is present; it only bootstraps Rust (defaulting to `stable`) when
`cargo` is entirely absent, so the standalone `rake` binary still works on a
bare machine.

With `toolchain` `Some(channel)`: when `cargo` is absent and stdin is an
interactive terminal, the user is prompted to install Rust via rustup
(defaulting to `channel`). When `cargo` is present but `channel` is not an
installed toolchain, the user is prompted to install that channel via rustup.
Once available, the process is pinned to `channel` (via `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`)
so the commands it spawns use the requested channel. When rustup is not
managing the toolchain (e.g. a distro-packaged cargo), the existing `cargo`
is accepted as-is.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ Error::RustToolchainMissing](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.RustToolchainMissing) when

`cargo` is absent and install is
declined or impossible (no interactive terminal);
[when the requested channel is absent and installing it is declined or impossible;](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.RustChannelMissing)

`Error::RustChannelMissing`[/](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.RustInstallSpawn)

`Error::RustInstallSpawn`[when an installer cannot be launched or exits non-zero; or](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.RustInstallFailed)

`Error::RustInstallFailed`[if reading a prompt response fails.](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.Io)

`Error::Io`

---

# format_duration in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.format_duration.html

## Expand description

Format `elapsed` with microsecond precision, promoting the unit as the value
grows: `µs`, then `ms`, then `s`, then composite `min`/`s` at the top tier.
Every tier carries exactly [`FRAC_DIGITS`] digits after the decimal,
zero-padded, with the integer part space-padded to [`INT_WIDTH`], e.g.
` 523.00000 µs`, `   1.01000 ms`, `   1.50100 s`, `1 min   30.50000 s`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::time::Duration;
use librake::format_duration;
assert_eq!(format_duration(Duration::from_micros(100)),      " 100.00000 µs");
assert_eq!(format_duration(Duration::from_micros(1_000)),    "   1.00000 ms");
assert_eq!(format_duration(Duration::from_secs(1)),          "   1.00000 s");
assert_eq!(format_duration(Duration::from_micros(90_500_000)), "1 min   30.50000 s");
```

---

# list_targets in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.list_targets.html

## Expand description

Render the targets of `rakefile` for display, in declaration order.

Platform-specific variants are resolved at parse time, so only the matched
variant’s commands appear. For each target the output shows the target name;
`depends_on` and `tools` summaries; and each command’s name and body (cmd or
shell variants) with per-command `(platform: …)`/`(arch: …)`/`(tools: …)`/`(skip_on_error)` markers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use librake::{Rakefile, list_targets};
let toml = "[[target.build.command]]\nname=\"compile\"\ncmd=[\"cargo\",\"build\"]";
let rakefile = Rakefile::from_toml_str(toml)?;
let out = list_targets(&rakefile);
assert!(out.contains("build"));
assert!(out.contains("compile"));
assert!(out.contains("cargo build"));
```
Platform-specific variants are resolved at parse time; only the matching variant (or base) appears in the output:

```
use librake::{Rakefile, list_targets};
let toml = r#"
[[target.sign.command]]
name = "notarize"
cmd  = ["xcrun", "notarytool", "submit"]
"#;
let rakefile = Rakefile::from_toml_str(toml)?;
let out = list_targets(&rakefile);
assert!(out.contains("sign"), "got: {out}");
assert!(out.contains("notarize"), "got: {out}");
```
A command with command-level tools shows a `(tools: …)` marker:

```
use librake::{Rakefile, list_targets};
let toml = r#"
[tool.os.docker]
check = ["docker", "--version"]
[[target.build.command]]
name  = "package"
cmd   = ["docker", "build", "."]
tools = ["docker"]
"#;
let rakefile = Rakefile::from_toml_str(toml)?;
let out = list_targets(&rakefile);
assert!(out.contains("(tools: docker)"), "got: {out}");
```

---

# load_license in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.load_license.html

`pub fn load_license() -> `[Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[LicensePayload](https://docs.rs/struct.LicensePayload.html)>>## Expand description

Load a license for the `run` path, printing a `Licensed` status line on
success.

Resolution order: `RAKE_LICENSE` env var → platform config file.  Returns
`Ok(None)` when no key is configured (including when the placeholder key is
still in place).  Hard-fails on an invalid `RAKE_LICENSE` value; soft-fails
(warns) on a corrupt or expired config file.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns [ Error::LicenseMalformed](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.LicenseMalformed) when the verifying key bytes are
invalid, and propagates

[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.LicenseMalformed)

`Error::LicenseMalformed`[, or](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.LicenseInvalidSignature)

`Error::LicenseInvalidSignature`[when](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html#variant.LicenseExpired)

`Error::LicenseExpired``RAKE_LICENSE` is set but the key fails verification.

# print_runtime in librake - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/librake/0.5.0/librake/fn.print_runtime.html

## Expand description

Print `label` (right-justified into the shared [`LABEL_WIDTH`] column,
bold-green when stderr is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is unset) followed by the
[ format_duration](https://docs.rs/fn.format_duration.html) rendering of

`elapsed`. Justifying to the shared width
lines the times up with the command/tool status lines and across the
per-command `Cmd Runtime` and final `Runtime` lines. Write errors are
ignored — this output is best-effort.

Print a blank separator followed by one Updated or Installed status
line per UpdateRecord, using [print_label] so the labels align in the
shared status column. Does nothing when updates is empty.

# sim_citizen_derive - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-citizen-derive/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Proc macros for SIM citizen values.

`#[derive(Citizen)]` generates the citizen support for a domain type from its
`#[citizen(...)]` attributes (symbol, version, and field options), and the
`#[non_citizen]` attribute marks a type as an explicit, descriptor-named
exemption. The generated code targets the `sim-citizen` support layer.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [non_](https://docs.rs/attr.non_citizen.html)- citizen
- Marks a type as an explicit non-citizen exemption.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Citizen](https://docs.rs/derive.Citizen.html)
- Derives the SIM citizen support for a domain type.

# sim_lib_audio_graph_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-audio-graph-core/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Pure Rust audio processor graph primitives.

The core graph is hardware-free: callers provide processors, prepare the graph, and can render deterministic offline blocks in tests or previews.

```
use sim_lib_audio_graph_core::{
    Graph, PrepareConfig, ProcessBlock, Processor,
};
#[derive(Default)]
struct CopyNode;
impl Processor for CopyNode {
    fn prepare(&mut self, _cfg: PrepareConfig) {}
    fn reset(&mut self) {}
    fn process(&mut self, block: &mut ProcessBlock<'_>) {
        let frames = block.frames as usize;
        for (input, output) in block.in_audio.iter().zip(block.out_audio.iter_mut()) {
            output[..frames].copy_from_slice(&input[..frames]);
        }
    }
}
let mut graph = Graph::new();
graph.add_node("copy", Box::<CopyNode>::default(), 1, 1).unwrap();
graph.prepare(48_000, 4).unwrap();
let output = graph.process_offline(&[vec![0.25, -0.5]], 2).unwrap();
assert_eq!(output, vec![vec![0.25, -0.5]]);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Audio](https://docs.rs/struct.AudioGraphNodeConfig.html)- Graph - Node - Config
- Citizen descriptor wrapping a single `PatchNode`
- [Audio](https://docs.rs/struct.AudioGraphPatchDescriptor.html)- Graph - Patch - Descriptor
- Citizen descriptor wrapping a whole `Patch`
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockArena.html)- Arena
- Bump allocator for per-block `f32`scratch buffers.
- [Bridge](https://docs.rs/struct.BridgeLatency.html)- Latency
- Latency a bridge incurs, measured in frames and packets.
- [Cable](https://docs.rs/struct.Cable.html)
- A directed connection from one node’s output port to another’s input port.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainBridgeDescriptor.html)- Bridge - Descriptor
- Full description of one domain bridge: its kind, the input and output rate contracts it joins, the latency it costs, and its diagnostic symbols.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainBridgeProcessor.html)- Bridge - Processor
- A `Processor`

- A directed audio processor graph: nodes plus the cables between their ports.

- An `EventSink`

- Portable, serializable description of a graph: its nodes and cables.

- Portable description of one graph node: its id and channel counts.

# sim_value - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-value/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Ergonomic construction and access for kernel `Expr` data.

The kernel `Expr` enum is bare data with no ergonomic surface, so dozens of
libs independently re-grew `sym`/`number`/`field`/`set`/`expr_kind` and a
`k`/`i` path-addressing scheme. This crate is the one home for that. It
depends only on `sim-kernel` and adds data ergonomics, not runtime behavior,
so it does not touch the kernel boundary.

- `build`- `sym`,- `int`,- `float`,- `text`,- `list`,- `map`, …);
- `access`- `field`,- `set`,- `remove`, …);
- `kind`- `Expr`variant classifier (- `expr_kind`);
- `path`- `Path`,- `get`,- `set_at`).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use sim_value::access::{field, set};
use sim_value::build::{int, map, sym};
let value = map(vec![("a", int(1)), ("b", int(2))]);
assert_eq!(field(&value, "a"), Some(&int(1)));
let updated = set(&value, "a", int(9));
assert_eq!(field(&updated, "a"), Some(&int(9)));
assert_eq!(field(&updated, "b"), Some(&int(2))); // siblings preserved
let _ = sym("ok");
```

---

# sim_lib_daw_session - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-daw-session/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_daw_session/index.html

## Expand description

Headless DAW session surface for SIM audio graph workspaces.

Sessions are portable data: an audio graph `Patch` plus tracks, buses,
clips, transport, plugin-chain state, and recording metadata. The crate is
hardware-free and can render deterministic offline buffers for tests,
previews, and agent inspection.

```
use sim_lib_daw_session::{
    DawClip, DawSession, DawTrack, daw_session_topology_package,
    render_session_offline,
};
let mut session = DawSession::new("doc", "Doc Session", 48_000).unwrap();
let track = DawTrack::audio("lead", "Lead", 2)
    .unwrap()
    .with_clip(DawClip::constant("tone", 0, 4, 0.25).unwrap());
session.add_track(track).unwrap();
let render = render_session_offline(&session, 4).unwrap();
assert_eq!(render.tracks_rendered(), 1);
assert_eq!(render.clips_rendered(), 1);
let package = daw_session_topology_package(&session);
assert_eq!(package.tests.len(), 1);
```

- Mix bus metadata.
- [DawClip](https://docs.rs/struct.DawClip.html)

### impl [DawSession](https://docs.rs/struct.DawSession.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sim_lib_daw_session/model.rs.html#59-222)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-DawSession-2)### impl [DawSession](https://docs.rs/struct.DawSession.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sim_lib_daw_session/model.rs.html#59-222)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-DawSession-2)

### impl [DawSession](https://docs.rs/struct.DawSession.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sim_lib_daw_session/model.rs.html#73-100)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sim_lib_daw_session/model.rs.html#73-100)

Creates an empty session with a single stereo `master` bus.

Fails if the id or name is empty or the sample rate is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sim_lib_daw_session::DawSession;
let session = DawSession::new("set", "My Set", 48_000).unwrap();
assert_eq!(session.sample_rate_hz(), 48_000);
assert_eq!(session.buses().len(), 1);
```

# DawSessionDescriptor in sim_lib_daw_session - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-daw-session/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_daw_session/struct.DawSessionDescriptor.html

`pub struct DawSessionDescriptor { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Citizen descriptor that carries a [ DawSession](https://docs.rs/struct.DawSession.html) as a runtime object.

The session is stored in its [ Expr](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/expr/enum.Expr.html) encoding so it can round-trip through
the citizen protocol;

[decodes it back.](https://docs.rs/struct.DawSessionDescriptor.html#method.session)

`DawSessionDescriptor::session`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)
